content.user_title: Plan Compliant Cross-Border Data Asset Projects
content.value_statement: Cross-border data asset projects must satisfy overlapping foreign exchange, data, securities, and local-law requirements. This skill coordinates specialized reviews into one structured compliance plan.
actual_capabilities: Routes project questions across five specialist roles for financing, tokenization, trade finance, commodities, and data export.
Compares cross-border pathways against foreign exchange, data, securities, and foreign-law gates.
Assesses data export scenarios, exemption conditions, and available compliance routes.
Structures workflows for trade finance, RWA tokenization, and commodity-backed digital asset projects.
Produces deliverable lists, phased plans, quality checks, and regulatory risk warnings.
Identifies prohibited domestic token issuance, improper investor sales, false trade financing, and return guarantees.
limitations: It does not replace advice from licensed lawyers, securities firms, banks, auditors, or regulators.
Policy references may become outdated and require verification against current official sources.
It cannot confirm asset ownership, transaction authenticity, regulatory approval, or financing success.
Recommendations depend on complete facts about assets, jurisdictions, investors, data, and transaction structure.

use_cases.title: Screen a Data Asset Financing Plan
use_cases.description: Compare possible offshore financing routes and identify required reviews, filings, and professional participants.

use_cases.title: Assess a Data Export Scenario
use_cases.description: Classify the transfer scenario, test possible exemptions, and outline the appropriate compliance route.
use_cases.target_user: Privacy, legal, and data governance teams

use_cases.title: Review a Tokenization Concept
use_cases.description: Identify domestic prohibitions, offshore legal dependencies, investor restrictions, and evidence required before detailed design.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Compliance Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project: [project summary]. List the foreign exchange, data, securities, and foreign-law questions we must answer first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an initial project screening.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Cross-Border Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable cross-border financing pathways for [asset and objective]. State prerequisites, regulators, key documents, timing assumptions, and disqualifying conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after basic project facts are available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Data Export Workplan
prompt_templates.prompt: For [data types, volume, subjects, recipient, jurisdiction, and purpose], assess exemption eligibility and compare available data export compliance routes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when overseas transfer or access is expected.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Integrated Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased review for [transaction]. Route tasks across all relevant specialists, define dependencies, list deliverables, and add stop conditions and quality checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced multi-domain project planning.

output_examples.input: A Chinese company wants overseas investors to finance a domestic data asset.
output: Initial route comparison with stated assumptions
Data export and foreign exchange workstreams
Required professional opinions and approval dependencies
Stop conditions for prohibited or unsupported structures

output_examples.input: An overseas affiliate needs remote access to customer records stored in China.
output: Transfer scenario and data classification questions
Comparison of security assessment, standard contract, and certification routes

output_examples.input: A project team proposes tokenizing gold inventory for offshore investors.
output: Evidence checklist for ownership, reserves, and valuation
Data, commodity, foreign exchange, and investor restriction workstreams

best_practices: Provide asset ownership, cash flow, jurisdictions, investor profile, data categories, and proposed transaction structure.
Verify every policy reference, deadline, threshold, and filing requirement with current official sources.
Treat legal, data, foreign exchange, and securities approvals as independent gates with documented owners.
anti_patterns: Do not request a definitive approval prediction from incomplete project facts.
Do not use the output as a substitute for licensed legal, financial, or regulatory advice.
Do not design domestic token fundraising, false trade financing, guaranteed returns, or sales to prohibited investors.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It organizes issues, workflows, and evidence for review by qualified professionals and relevant authorities.

faq.question: Can it determine whether a data export exemption applies?
faq.answer: It can perform a preliminary assessment from supplied facts. Current rules and project evidence still require professional verification.

faq.question: Does it support RWA tokenization projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies structural questions, offshore dependencies, investor restrictions, and domestic regulatory red lines.

faq.question: Can it guarantee regulatory approval or financing?
faq.answer: No. It cannot guarantee approvals, registrations, legal opinions, investment, transaction completion, or project timing.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide asset ownership, cash flow, locations, data categories, recipient details, investor profile, financing objective, and proposed jurisdictions.

faq.question: How should policy citations be used?
faq.answer: Confirm each citation, effective date, threshold, and local interpretation through current official publications and qualified advisers.
